title: Reinforcement Learning
html:
Reinforcement learning (RL) solves an MDP without knowing its transition model or reward function: the agent learns from trial and error, guided only by rewards. It powers game-playing agents, robotics controllers and the RLHF stage of LLM training.

Exploration vs exploitation

An agent that always takes the best-known action (exploit) may never discover a better one; one that always tries new actions (explore) never cashes in. ε-greedy explores with probability ε. A 3-armed bandit with win rates 0.2, 0.5 and 0.7:

Temporal-difference learning and Q-learning

TD learning updates an estimate towards a one-step bootstrapped target after every transition — no need to wait for the episode to end, and no model required:

TD(0): U(s) ← U(s) + α [ r + γ U(s′) − U(s) ]
Q-learning: Q(s, a) ← Q(s, a) + α [ r + γ · maxₐ′ Q(s′, a′) − Q(s, a) ]
SARSA: Q(s, a) ← Q(s, a) + α [ r + γ · Q(s′, a′) − Q(s, a) ] (a′ = the action actually taken next)

Q-learning is off-policy: it learns the value of the greedy policy while behaving ε-greedily. SARSA is on-policy: it learns the value of the policy it actually follows, exploration included. The classic cliff walking grid shows the difference — walk from the bottom-left to the bottom-right corner; stepping into the cliff between them costs −100 and restarts:

Key point

Q-learning learns the optimal path along the cliff edge, but with ε-greedy exploration it occasionally slips off while training. SARSA accounts for its own exploration and prefers a safer route — lower optimal-path quality, higher reward during learning.

Scaling up: deep RL

RLHF (2022–)A reward model trained on human preferences, optimised with PPO-style RL, aligns LLMs (see Generative AI)
Watch out

Reward hacking: an RL agent optimises the reward you wrote, not the one you meant — a boat-racing agent learned to spin in circles collecting points instead of finishing the race. Reward design is part of AI safety (see AI Ethics, Safety & Fairness).

How does reinforcement learning differ from supervised learning?

There are no labelled correct actions — only scalar rewards, often delayed. The agent's own actions determine what data it sees, so it must balance exploration and exploitation and solve credit assignment (which earlier action earned a later reward).

Q-learning vs SARSA?

Both are TD methods learning Q(s, a). Q-learning is off-policy — its target uses max Q(s′, ·), the greedy action — so it learns the optimal policy regardless of exploration. SARSA is on-policy — its target uses the action actually taken next — so it learns the value of the exploring policy and behaves more cautiously (cliff walking).

What is the exploration–exploitation trade-off? Name some strategies.

Exploiting uses current knowledge to maximise reward now; exploring gathers information that may pay off later. Strategies: ε-greedy (often with ε decaying), softmax/Boltzmann exploration, optimism in the face of uncertainty (optimistic initial values, UCB), and Thompson sampling.
